principle_text: When the seller sets a firm price, you should strategically increase your offer while offering additional value, such as self-pickup, to strengthen your position in negotiation.
When the seller confirms no scratches on the furniture, avoid revealing potential leverage points for justifying a lower price to maintain a strong bargaining position.
When the seller emphasizes the item's value and uniqueness, avoid asking for a price reduction without acknowledging these qualities, as it may undermine the seller's confidence in the product.
When the seller emphasizes the uniqueness and antique value of an item, avoid making significantly low offers that may signal desperation and weaken your negotiating position.
When the seller has already indicated the item's features and condition, you should anchor your offer close to your target price to prompt a price reduction during negotiation.

When the seller emphasizes a higher price and additional services, avoid increasing your offer without gaining any concessions in return, as it may weaken your bargaining position and lead to a less favorable outcome.
When the seller offers a lower price than their initial ask, avoid immediately accepting the offer without attempting to negotiate for a better deal.
When the seller emphasizes the high quality and condition of the item, avoid increasing the price after the buyer makes a concession, as it can weaken the buyer's position in the negotiation.
When the seller offers to add value by removing paint from the item, avoid making significantly lowball offers as it may weaken your negotiation position and lead to a higher counteroffer.
When the seller mentions an item's imperfection and lists it at a discounted price, you should leverage that imperfection to negotiate a lower price effectively.

When the seller has initially offered a higher price for a valuable item, you should gradually negotiate closer to the buyer's requested amount to show flexibility and reach a mutually beneficial agreement.
When the seller emphasizes the item's good condition and minimizes concerns about vintage wear, avoid probing for flaws to justify a lower offer.

When the seller emphasizes the vintage authenticity of an item instead of addressing restoration concerns, avoid inadvertently shifting the negotiation focus towards the item's value as a restorable vintage piece rather than its current functionality.
When the seller emphasizes the vintage nature and potential for buyer customization of an item, you should anchor your negotiation with a significantly lower offer to create room for price reduction.

When the seller reassures about the item's condition and offers additional free items, avoid shifting the focus away from negotiating the price directly to prevent diluting the buyer's negotiation strength.

When the seller mentions including additional items like wood filler and polish, avoid accepting the offer without negotiating further on the price to maintain leverage and prevent finalizing the deal at a higher initial price.

When the seller responds neutrally to the buyer's delay tactic of requesting more information before making an offer, avoid prolonging the negotiation without introducing specific leverage or a concrete counteroffer.

When the seller reiterates existing condition details without offering a price concession, avoid asking neutral informational questions unrelated to price to prevent stalling the negotiation progress.
When the seller has already lowered the price and offered a cash-only deal, avoid making aggressive offers and adding urgency, as it may backfire by reducing your leverage in the negotiation.
When the seller has not yet responded to a buyer's offer, avoid lowering the proposed price as it may prioritize closing the deal over securing the best possible terms in the negotiation.
When the seller offers to deliver and suggests a price close to the buyer's initial offer, you should assertively push for your target price to strengthen your negotiation position.

When the seller emphasizes the item's positive attributes like sturdiness, avoid asking questions that do not directly contribute to negotiating a lower price, as it may strengthen the seller's position without benefiting the buyer's negotiation stance.
When the seller shows willingness to accept a lower offer without negotiation, you should confidently propose a reduced price to secure a better deal.

When the seller shows willingness to negotiate by offering a lower price, you should creatively frame your price negotiation using diplomatic language and references to shared values for a more harmonious outcome.
When the seller emphasizes unique features of the item, avoid shifting the focus to non-price related topics like delivery, as it may not lead to immediate price concessions.

When the seller emphasizes unique features and agrees to the buyer's terms without negotiating further on price, avoid prematurely accepting the deal to maintain negotiation leverage and aim for a lower price.
When the seller provides a straightforward reason for selling an item, avoid emphasizing their urgency or using it as leverage to negotiate a lower price.
When highlighting a repair issue, you should leverage it as a negotiation point to request a lower price for the item.

When the seller has already reduced the price once and the buyer reasserts their target price with added urgency and immediate payment, you should offer immediate agreement to close the deal at the optimal price.
When the buyer emphasizes self-pickup and willingness to handle repairs, you should consider accepting their initial price offer to secure the sale with reduced effort on your part.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate by reducing the price, you should anchor the negotiation with a lower target price to gain immediate leverage and move closer to your desired deal.
When the seller has already offered a discounted price and delivery, you should strategically compromise by increasing your offer slightly to bridge the gap and maintain negotiation momentum.
When the seller immediately accepts a price below their initial price without negotiation, you should make a specific and slightly lower cash offer to secure a better deal.

When the seller counters with a price above your offer but shows willingness to negotiate, you should anchor firmly with a clear budget to establish leverage and guide the negotiation toward your target price.
When the seller counters by raising the price back to the buyer's initial offer while adding conditions, avoid lowering your offer below your original price as it weakens your negotiation leverage.

When the seller confirms the item's condition but a specific functional drawback affects your use, you should highlight that drawback and directly ask for their lowest price to leverage a better deal.
When the seller confirms the item's functionality without addressing price concerns, avoid shifting focus away from price or concessions to unrelated product features.
When the seller emphasizes the item's excellent condition and reiterates a firm price, avoid asking questions that allow the seller to strengthen their position and reduce your leverage.
When the seller maintains a firm initial price but shows willingness to negotiate, you should make a clear, direct low offer to prompt the seller to lower their price and possibly add concessions.
When the seller confirms product quality and reiterates their price, avoid asking only general product questions that do not apply pressure or advance price negotiation.
When the seller states a firm price but shows openness to negotiation, you should offer a lower price combined with immediate purchase or pickup to increase the likelihood of acceptance.

When the seller responds with a moderate price reduction and adds value, you should make a reasonable initial offer that encourages concessions without pushing too far below the seller’s initial price.
When the seller confirms limited quantity or incomplete items without price concessions, you should ask clarifying questions to identify negotiation leverage points.
When the seller provides straightforward factual information without indicating price flexibility, avoid asking purely informational questions that do not advance price negotiation.

When the seller firmly rejects a low offer but counters with a significantly reduced price and added conditions, you should use a lower anchor offer to create leverage and prompt a more favorable counteroffer.
When the seller emphasizes the product's quality and durability in response to your inquiry, avoid asking questions that reinforce the seller's justification for a higher price.
When the seller has stated a firm initial price, avoid making offers that exceed or include additional costs without negotiating a lower base price first.
When the seller reaffirms the high quality and good condition of the item without lowering the price, avoid asking neutral questions that allow the seller to reinforce their price justification.
When the seller indicates a firm price but hints at flexibility with conditions, you should introduce cost-saving options like self-pickup to create leverage for negotiating a better price.
When the seller provides detailed information about the product and additional included items, avoid making purely informational inquiries that do not advance your position on price.
When the seller maintains a firm price but highlights product quality, you should offer a specific cash amount and convenience to encourage a favorable price reduction.
When the seller responds to a higher buyer offer by countering with an increased price and added conditions, avoid making large concessions early that weaken your negotiation leverage.
When the seller reveals minor flaws or limitations in the product, you should use these details to build leverage for negotiating a lower price.
When the seller maintains a firm price but highlights added value, you should make a reasonable lower offer and offer to handle logistics to create leverage for a better deal.
When the seller firmly maintains their price and rejects additional non-monetary offers, avoid repeating initial low offers without increasing monetary concessions or leverage.
When the seller offers a counterprice that meets halfway and adds value like assistance, you should explicitly state your target price and reference cheaper alternatives to encourage a better offer.
When the seller states a firm price but shows willingness to close quickly, you should offer a higher price with conditions like immediate cash payment to secure a better deal.
When the seller has already accepted your price offer and confirmed terms, avoid repeating confirmations without introducing new negotiation points or requests.

When the seller responds by confirming logistical details after a lower price offer with added incentives, you should include specific concessions like immediate payment and pickup to increase the chance of acceptance.

When the seller responds to a price offer by shifting focus to logistical concerns instead of addressing the price, avoid immediately conceding or changing your price without exploring the underlying negotiation opportunity.
When the seller emphasizes a higher value and product durability in response to a low offer, avoid making sudden lower price offers that widen the price gap and weaken your negotiation position.
When the seller states a firm but slightly negotiable price and acknowledges item quality, you should propose a reasonable counteroffer close to their price to encourage immediate acceptance.
When the seller has already agreed to a lower price, avoid simply acknowledging the agreement without attempting to negotiate further or add value to the deal.
When the seller provides detailed information affirming the item's condition and suitability, avoid asking only informational questions that do not directly challenge the price or create leverage.
When the seller indicates a firm price but shows some openness, you should directly ask for a price reduction to encourage negotiation and invite a counteroffer.
When the seller offers a reasonable counteroffer between their initial price and your offer, you should consider accepting it promptly to secure the deal and avoid prolonged negotiation.
When the seller provides factual information about the item without discussing price, avoid making purely informational inquiries that do not leverage this information to negotiate better terms.
When the seller acknowledges item flaws and the need for repairs, you should combine a lower price offer with a commitment to immediate pickup to increase the likelihood of acceptance.
When the seller states a product limitation affecting your intended use, you should highlight that limitation and offer a lower price to prompt a seller concession.
When the seller has clearly stated non-negotiable terms, avoid asking questions that do not create leverage or influence the price negotiation.
When the seller rejects a low initial offer and counters with a higher price, you should avoid anchoring too low early and instead make a more strategic offer to maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller responds to a low offer by slightly lowering the price but maintaining a high counteroffer, avoid increasing your offer prematurely as it weakens your negotiating leverage.

When the seller firmly states the price is non-negotiable and justifies it by emphasizing the handmade quality, avoid making lowball offers that highlight negative aspects without first acknowledging the item's value.
When the seller indicates a firm price with limited flexibility, avoid increasing your offer too quickly as it may reduce your leverage and encourage the seller to raise their counteroffer.
When the seller emphasizes the item's durability and quality without conceding on price, avoid asking questions that do not directly challenge the price or terms.
When the seller emphasizes minor imperfections as a reason for a higher price, you should leverage these flaws to justify a lower counteroffer.
When the seller agrees to a lower price contingent on buyer's conditions, you should accept the offer promptly to finalize the deal and secure the agreed terms without risking reversal.
When the seller confirms the item has no functional defects, avoid focusing on quality issues that do not create leverage for negotiating a lower price.

When the seller maintains firmness on price but shows willingness to negotiate, you should propose your target price along with a time-sensitive pickup offer to create urgency and encourage a price concession.
When the seller offers a conditional price reduction, you should assert your firm cash offer to encourage immediate acceptance without additional concessions.

When the seller responds with a counteroffer higher than the buyer's increased offer and adds extra value, avoid conceding too quickly or raising your offer prematurely, as it weakens your negotiating position.
When the seller immediately accepts a reasonable counteroffer without resistance, you should propose a fair but lower price to quickly secure a better deal.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition with no damage, avoid relying solely on condition concerns to justify a lower price.
When the seller firmly rejects a low initial offer and counters with a higher price, avoid making offers that are too low to be taken seriously as it weakens your negotiation position.

When the seller proposes a counteroffer with a higher price and an added service like delivery, you should accept the counteroffer price while offering to handle logistics yourself to secure a better deal.
When the seller maintains a firm initial price but shows willingness to negotiate with conditions, you should directly acknowledge the price as high and request a reduction to prompt a concession.
When the seller responds to a lowest price inquiry by revealing a defect but refuses to lower the price, avoid accepting the justification without pressing for a price reduction.
When the seller expresses pride in their work but is motivated to sell quickly, you should offer your target price along with incentives like immediate payment and pickup to encourage acceptance.
When the seller firmly rejects a very low offer, avoid making drastic price reductions that undermine your credibility and hinder constructive negotiation progress.
When the seller responds with a firm counteroffer closer to the buyer's offer, you should make a reasonable initial offer that anchors the negotiation toward your target price.

When the seller clearly states they cannot lower the price due to the item's excellent condition, avoid directly asking how low they are willing to go as it may reinforce their firm stance and reduce negotiation leverage.
When the seller emphasizes the item's value and firmness on price, you should make a reasonable counteroffer closer to their price to encourage a constructive counteroffer.
When the seller responds positively by accepting a lower price offer with specific conditions, you should propose a slightly reduced price to secure a better deal immediately.
When the seller reaffirms the item's quality and price without conceding, avoid making inquiries that do not directly address or challenge the price to maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller clearly states a price with added incentives contingent on payment terms, avoid ambiguous acceptance that finalizes the deal without attempting further price negotiation.
When the seller provides factual information about the item's condition and availability without adjusting price, avoid relying solely on informational questions to pressure for a lower price.
When the seller indicates flexibility by offering a lower price with conditions, you should appeal to personal circumstances to encourage a price reduction.
When the seller offers a price reduction contingent on removing add-ons, avoid immediately accepting the full original price including add-ons without negotiating further to maintain leverage.
When the seller holds firm on the initial price, avoid conceding to that price without negotiating further or leveraging additional terms to improve your position.
When the seller confirms acceptable payment methods without discussing price, avoid focusing on transactional details that do not advance price negotiation.
When the seller confirms product details without adjusting price or conceding, avoid asking purely informational questions that do not create leverage for negotiation.
When the seller maintains a firm initial price but shows willingness to reduce it slightly, you should make a reasonable counteroffer closer to their price to encourage downward movement.
